name: How to Evaluate Seismic Retrofit Contractor Bids in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What should Los Angeles County owners look for when comparing bids from seismic retrofit contractors beyond just the total price?
mainEntity.text: What should Los Angeles County owners look for when comparing bids from seismic retrofit contractors beyond just the total price?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing a seismic retrofit contractor in Los Angeles County requires more than selecting the lowest bid. Owners should analyze how each proposal addresses scope, risk, and local compliance to avoid unexpected costs and delays. First, verify the contractor’s specific experience with seismic retrofits under the relevant city or county ordinances and building type: soft-story wood-frame, non-ductile concrete, or hillside structures. Ask for completed project examples and references for buildings similar in size and configuration. Review the bid to see whether engineering design, permit submittals, plan check responses, and special inspections are included or treated as separate costs. Clarify which items are allowances versus fixed-price, and how unforeseen conditions such as foundation deterioration or utility conflicts will be handled. A detailed scope description should list the number and location of frames, shear walls, foundation elements, and finishes to be removed and patched. Confirm that protection of existing finishes, landscaping, and tenant areas is addressed. Evaluate proposed construction schedules and how work will be phased to minimize disruption. Ensure the contractor carries appropriate general liability and workers’ compensation insurance and understands any lender, HOA, or ownership reporting requirements. A transparent, well-documented bid with realistic contingencies and clear assumptions is often more valuable than a lower price that leaves key items unspecified.
acceptedAnswer.description: When comparing seismic retrofit bids in Los Angeles County, owners should evaluate contractor experience with local ordinances, inclusion of engineering and permits, clarity of scope, allowances for unforeseen conditions, schedule commitments, insurance, and references on similar buildings. Lowest price alone can hide exclusions that lead to costly change orders later.
